verdicts.reason: The repo matches the claim. E-2 has only `needs: {edu: 3}` and no `countries`, and 13 visas lead to it (D-2-2/3/4, D-4-1, D-10-1, F-3, NONE and others), so it shows as OPEN for every nationality. verified-by-review.md already lists this under Confirmed WRONG #1. The legal rule is right for English: E-2-1 needs citizenship of the country whose language you teach, and for English that means the 7 designated countries. A Korean bachelor's only counts if you finished high school or college in that country. Saying such students can 'never' get E-2 goes too far: anyone may teach the language of their own country, and Indian nationals may have a CEPA English-assistant route (E-2-91). The fix needs changing. The gate belongs on the E-2 visa itself, not on the D-2 moves, because a move's own `needs` would not cover the other 10 incoming routes; a visa-level `countries` check runs separately from `needs`. The group must also be a concrete list instead of '...'. I could not re-fetch the manual (no network); this relies on the 2026 manual entries recorded in visadocs.yaml and on the earlier review.

In data/visamap.yaml:
groups:
  e2Native: [US, GB, CA, ZA, NZ, AU, IE, CN, TW, HK, JP, FR, BE, CH, DE, AT, ES, MX, AR, CO, CL, PE, IT, PT, BR, RU, VN, TH, ID, MN]
E-2:
  countries: e2Native      # keep needs: {edu: 3}
  how.en: append "Other languages: only the language of your own country, with a degree from that country (or high school or college there and a Korean bachelor's)."  (ru, uz and uz-cyrl must be translated)
Do NOT add per-move needs/countries on the D-2-2/D-2-3/D-2-4 -> E-2 moves; the visa-level gate covers all of them.

verdicts.reason: The repo's D-2-7 name is 'Work-study student' and its how is 'Degree program linked with work in Korea, including GKS students'. That is a literal reading of the code name 일-학습연계. The MOJ student guideline instead defines D-2-7 by who holds it: students selected for a GKS government scholarship, a foreign government's full-tuition scholarship, or a university's full-tuition STEM scholarship, studying in a regular Korean degree course from associate degree up. 'Linked with work' is the policy goal, which is preferential treatment after graduation, not a feature of the course. Two separate research passes (this finding and the D-2-7 gives research in the scratchpad) quote the same definition, and it matches my own recollection. I could not re-open the PDF (no network). The fix must change all four languages, not only `.en`.
verdicts.correctedFix:
In data/visamap.yaml D-2-7:
  name.en: "Scholarship student (GKS etc.)"
  how.en: "A regular Korean degree course (associate to doctorate) on a full scholarship: a GKS government scholarship, a foreign government's full-tuition scholarship, or a university's full-tuition STEM scholarship."
(name.ru/uz/uz-cyrl and how.ru/uz/uz-cyrl must be translated to match.)

verdicts.reason: The repo does say KIIP 3 / TOPIK 3 for F-2-R. But the 2025 press release the finding relies on, which raised the level to 4, is no longer the rule in force. The 2026.9.18 sojourn manual's F-2-R change-of-status document list (stored in data/visadocs.yaml) asks for KIIP level-3 completion (or a pre-test placement at level 4+) or TOPIK 3+. An earlier agent read the full text of 법무부고시 제2026-248호 제4조제1항 (finding f2#5) and reports the same: KIIP stage 3+ or TOPIK 3+. Finding d10#6 also notes a relaxation to TOPIK 3 effective 2026-08-03. So the current `lang: {topik: 3, kiip: 3}`, the F-2-R how and the D-10-1 -> F-2-R note are correct for 2026. Raising them to 4 would be wrong.

verdicts.reason: The repo matches the claim: D-2-6 and D-2-8 offer only D-2-2 and D-2-3, both as `abroad: true` with the note 'Usually after the exchange ends...'. An exchange or visiting student can certainly go on to an associate or doctoral course. At minimum this works from abroad, since D-2-1 and D-2-4 both have abroad issuance lists in the 2026.9.1 visa manual, and D-2-4's own `needs: {edu: 4}` already gates the doctorate. The fix contradicts itself: it says 'as in-Korea changes' while the D-2-2/D-2-3 entries it copies are currently abroad. Making them in-Korea depends on d2#0/d2#1 being accepted. The new entries should simply copy whatever flag and note the D-2-2/D-2-3 entries end up with.

verdicts.reason: The repo does have no `gives` on D-2-5. But a master's degree is required only in principle, not by definition. The 2026.9.1 visa manual's D-2-5 document list says '석사학위이상 소지자를 원칙으로 함' (in principle), and a course-specific note also allows home-country bachelor's students invited for STEM research by a designated research university or a top-ranked (THE 200 / QS 500) Korean university. That exception is exactly why the repo has `needs: [{edu: 4}, {stem: true}]`. Adding `gives: {edu: 4}` would wrongly give those undergraduates a master's for later steps and unlock E-3, which needs edu 4. Today an undergraduate on D-2-5 is correctly kept out of E-3.

verdicts.reason: The repo matches the claim: no D-2 code leads to D-4-1, whose only in-Korea incoming route is G-1-6. The guideline separates language study done as part of a degree course, which needs no change of status, from leaving the degree course (leave of absence or a tuition refund) to enrol in a separate language course, which does. D-4-1 has an in-Korea change document list in the 2026.9.18 manual. That list includes an 'enrolment certificate or highest-education' item and a 'why language training is needed' item for registered foreigners, which fits a change from another long-term status. So the in-Korea move can be expressed in this engine. I could not re-fetch the guideline (no network), but the quoted rule matches my recollection of the D-2/D-4 sections. The note must be added in all four languages.

verdicts.reason: In the repo, D-2-2 has no downward move and D-2-3 offers only D-2-2, so D-2-1 cannot be reached from any higher course. The repo's own visadocs.yaml `within` table, built from the 2026.9.18 sojourn manual section on exceptional moves to a lower degree course, lists D-2-2>D-2-1 and D-2-3>D-2-1 as use: report. D-2-1 carries the matching report document list (TOPIK 3 proof, standard admission letter, etc.). The same mechanism already backs the D-2-3>D-2-2, D-2-4>D-2-2 and D-2-4>D-2-3 moves in the map. The existing 'moving down' note is already in all four languages and fits word for word, so the fix can copy it.
